name: FreeDuel_PlaceCursor
notes: Name from module-scoped external symbols; exact boundary from the verified overlay split. Places the cursor widget at x D_8009B366 * 56 + 20 and y D_8009B367 * 52 + 40 then calls func_80035B7C with D_800EB0F8; when the second argument is set it indexes gFreeDuel_abGridAvailable by D_8009B36C + D_8009B367 * 5 and if that byte is set writes the index minus 31960 to D_8009B32E, copies a pair of s16 from D_801D0000 + index * 4 + 1820 into the two words at D_801D5608 when the index is non-zero, and calls func_80035BE4 and func_80039A60. Reconstructed to 73 of 73 instructions with 5 differing positions under gcc_2_8_1_g0_split. Levers: D_8009B366 and D_8009B367 read into locals before the coordinate stores; the truncated value in its own s16 while the argument stays s32; and the D_801D0000 base and the address of D_8009B32E each named in a local before the arithmetic that uses them which moves their %hi ahead of it. The scheduling-flag question is closed: against this candidate gcc_2_8_1_g0_split_no_sched1 gcc_2_8_1_g0_no_sched2_split gcc_2_8_1_g0_no_sched2 and gcc_2_8_1_g0_no_sched1 differ at 57 54 66 and 72 positions. What remains is the leading pair of lui instructions; the same local-naming trick does not reach it because D_8009B366 is already read first and D_800EB0F8 is held in a callee-saved register across two calls. Reconstructed again from this note alone and the ambiguous lever cost thirteen positions: read into locals before the coordinate stores means both coordinates are read before either store not each one before its own store. Reading the column then storing x then reading the row then storing y builds 73 of 73 with eighteen differing positions because the row load can no longer move up into the column arithmetic; hoisting both reads together restores the five-position shape. The if-else for the call argument is also an override not a choice: param equals the truncated value first and then the non-zero arm overwrites it with 12 which puts the sign extension in the branch delay slot - written as a genuine else it builds 74. Retested against this corrected shape and still not helping: profiles gcc_2_8_1_g0_no_sched2_split gcc_2_8_1_g0_split_no_sched1 gcc_2_8_1_g8_split and gcc_2_8_1_cc_g8_as_g0_split differ at 73 58 72 and 67 positions so the scheduling-flag question stays closed on the better candidate too; the widget parameter retyped to s16 pointer with element indexing changes nothing; s16 locals for the coordinates build 75; and the panel local can be assigned first last or not at all - four placements all give the same five positions which confirms the residual is not reachable by naming it.

name: FreeDuel_Init
notes: Name from module-scoped external symbols; exact boundary from the verified overlay split. Pre-flight is clean: no jump table, no frame pointer prologue and no frame-bound block copy, so this is an ordinary candidate on the usual profile. The opening is decoded and both halves check against the game notes. When bit 0x80 of gFreeDuel_bReturnFlags is set it records the result of the duel just played: it forms a u16 pointer into D_801D071C at index D_8009B367 times 5 plus D_8009B366 scaled by 4, advances it by one halfword when D_8009B362 is 1, then increments the halfword and clamps it to 999. D_801D071C is the 40 entry table of u16 wins and u16 losses documented in section 12 of the game notes, so the conditional halfword step is what selects losses over wins. It then clears the viewport origin, and on a cold entry with no return flags plays the intro through func_80035C38 and func_80039794 and sets bit 0x20 of gFreeDuel_bScreenFlags. It clears the sixteen entries of gFreeDuel_apSparklePool from the top down, fills the forty bytes of gFreeDuel_abGridAvailable with 1 from the top down, then walks ids 1 to 38 calling func_8002CCA8 with 0x6E0 plus the id and clearing the byte when the call returns zero. That constant is the Free Duel unlocked flag base from section 12, which confirms the grid is gated on the per-duelist unlock bits. The remainder, from the func_80082324 wait onward, is texture upload through nested five by five loops calling func_80081DE8 and has not been decoded yet.

name: FreeDuel_UpdateSparkle
notes: Exact overlay match with gcc_2_8_1_g0_split. Scans the sixteen entries of gFreeDuel_apSparklePool from 15 down to 0; an entry whose low nibble at +0x6C is 1 gets bit 0x80 set once and is then initialised with timer 16 at +0x60 colour 0x404040 as a word at +0xC and flag 0x50000000 or-ed into +0x4. Every frame the three colour bytes at +0xE +0xD +0xC fade by 4 and the timer counts down; at zero it calls func_8004036C and clears the slot. Two levers: the decremented timer goes into a named s16 local because reading obj->timer again for the test reloads it and costs an instruction and the sll 16 test comes from the local being signed; and the timer statement is written after the three colour stores. The transposition recorded here as a scheduler choice was that second point: swapping the two adjacent statements is byte-identical because it changes no dependence but moving one past the stores does.

name: FreeDuel_UpdateCursorTween
notes: Name from module-scoped external symbols; exact boundary from the verified overlay split. Slides the cursor widget in gFreeDuel_pCursorWidget from the current grid cell in D_8009B366 and D_8009B367 to the target in D_8009B36C and D_8009B36D. While bit 0x40 of gFreeDuel_bScreenFlags is clear it returns at once if both coordinates already agree; otherwise it sets that bit, writes 8 to the frame count at +0x60, calls func_800429D8 and stores per-frame steps at +0x36 and +0x38 as target minus current shifted left 8 and divided by 8 using the same 8.8 fixed point as func_801689B4. The target coordinates use the same formulas as FreeDuel_PlaceCursor: row * 56 + 20 and column * 52 + 40. Every frame it advances through func_80042A78 and decrements +0x60. At zero it copies the target cell into the current cell calls FreeDuel_PlaceCursor with 1 clears bit 0x40 and calls func_8003FEE0 with 47. Otherwise it takes a slot from FreeDuel_GetSparkleSlot and an object from FreeDuel_SpawnSparkle and when both are non-zero copies the widget's coordinate pair at +0x30 as one 32-bit word sets the sparkle's +0x6C to 1 and bit 1 of +0x8 copies +0x4C and publishes it into the slot. Measured: the step must be written as a division by 8 rather than a shift by 3 because the target has the bgez plus seven bias; that source builds 123 instructions against 120 while the shift form builds 115. Not yet identified: three instructions elsewhere, and the target fills the delay slot of the early-return branch with the widget pointer where the build leaves a nop. Since then: the target coordinate must be a named local so that plus twenty binds before the subtraction. Written inline as (row * 56 + 20) - current GCC re-associates it to row * 56 - (current - 20) and emits addiu -20 on the current position instead of addiu 20 on the target. With tx = row * 56 + 20 first the arithmetic block matches. The three surplus instructions are identified as unfilled delay slots rather than extra work: the target fills the early-return beq slot with the widget pointer and the first bgez slot with the %hi of the second coordinate's symbol while the build leaves nops in both. Hoisting both target coordinates above both step assignments goes the other way and builds 119; naming the raw coordinates first builds 122. Retested with the pointer-type and named-local levers: the shape now builds 121 instructions against 120 and two of the three recorded surplus nops are gone. The lever is that the first step must be computed into a named local and stored after the second target coordinate is read - with sx = ((tx minus the widget's x) shifted left 8) over 8 then ty = column * 52 + 40 then the store of sx GCC hoists the lb of D_8009B36D and its lui above the +0x36 store which fills the first bgez delay slot with that %hi and covers the lb's own load delay. Storing the first step immediately leaves both nops because the load cannot move above the store. Measured and not helping: hoisting both coordinates above both steps still builds 119; naming only the raw second coordinate builds 122; nesting the two early-return comparisons or inverting them to a disjunction with an else changes nothing; reading the flags byte twice instead of into a local changes nothing; a second local for the call argument changes nothing; calling func_800429D8 before the flag store builds 122; swapping the flag store and the +0x60 store keeps 121; dropping the widget local builds 125; and profiles gcc_2_8_1_g0_no_sched2_split gcc_2_8_1_g0_split_no_sched1 and gcc_2_8_1_g8_split are all worse. What remains is one nop: the target fills the early-return beq delay slot with the move of the widget into a0 - the argument for func_800429D8 - so that the copy appears in both branch delay slots and not in the block they converge on while the build fills only the first branch's slot and keeps the original. The delay slot residual is now read exactly and supersedes the looser description above. The target does not merely fill one slot: the same instruction, the copy of the widget pointer into a0 for func_800429D8, appears in the delay slots of both early comparisons - the bne that jumps into the tween block and the beq that returns - and does not appear in the block they converge on at all. That is the delay slot filler copying one instruction into both predecessors and then deleting the original because every path into the block now performs it. The build gets the first slot only, leaves a nop in the second and keeps the original, which is the single extra instruction. So what is wanted is not a different instruction in the second slot but the deletion of the original, which only happens once both predecessors carry it. Rebuilt from this note and improved from 121 instructions with one surplus nop to 120 of 120 with four differing positions. Two levers closed the gap. The read of the widget's +0x4C must be written above the stores through the sparkle rather than below them: a store through the sparkle pointer may alias the widget, so the scheduler cannot hoist the load itself, and left below it the load-use delay goes unfilled and costs a nop. Writing the +0x4C copy first and the +0x6C and +0x8 stores after it lets the scheduler sink the store instead, which is what the target shows. The second is that the delay slot reading recorded just above was not a separate defect at all: once that surplus nop at the end of the function was removed the delay slot of the early-return branch filled with the widget pointer on its own, both predecessors carried the copy and the original was deleted. So that residual was a symptom of a one instruction excess elsewhere rather than an independent problem, which is worth recording because it was an actively misleading search target. What remains is four positions and they are two copies of one register allocation choice: for both coordinate steps the target puts the subtraction result into the register that held the widget's current coordinate while the build puts it into the register that held the target coordinate, after which both free the same register for the next %hi. Measured and not helping: naming the current coordinate in a local before the subtraction, which builds 119 with eighty differing positions.

name: FreeDuel_UpdateScreen
notes: Name from module-scoped external symbols; exact overlay match with gcc_2_8_1_g0_split. Per-frame update for the Free Duel opponent select screen. While bit 0x20 of gFreeDuel_bScreenFlags is set a modal message is up: it pumps func_80039794 and waits for bit 3 of the u16 at +0x34 of D_800EB15C to clear before dropping the bit, calling func_80035B7C, setting 0x40 in the cursor widget's u16 at +8 and replacing the cursor through FreeDuel_PlaceCursor. Otherwise it advances FreeDuel_UpdateCursorTween and FreeDuel_UpdateScrollbar and ignores input while the tween bit 0x40 is set. The d-pad bits of D_8009B3A4 move the target cell not the current one: 0x2000 and 0x8000 step D_8009B36C over 0 to 4 and 0x4000 and 0x1000 step D_8009B36D over 0 to 7, each clamped by re-reading the stored byte as a signed char. The five by eight grid is the 40 Free Duel tiles and gFreeDuel_abGridAvailable is indexed D_8009B367 * 5 + D_8009B366 so an unavailable tile is rejected. Cell zero is the Build Deck tile per the-game.md section 12 which is why (D_8009B366 | D_8009B367) == 0 takes a separate path that calls func_80033C90, sets gFreeDuel_bReturnFlags to 0x40, and records the return screen 6 in D_8009B269. Any other tile scans the 40 u16 card ids of the deck at D_801D0200 and an empty slot opens a message box through func_80035C38 and sets 0x20 instead of starting the duel; a full deck sets gFreeDuel_bReturnFlags to 0x80, calls func_80024DC8 with the tile index and hands off with D_8009B26C = 3. Levers: func_80035B7C takes the panel pointer, so D_800EB15C has to be a named local used both for the +0x34 field test and as the call argument. Written as a direct symbol expression GCC folds +0x34 into the relocation and the base instruction disappears, building 205 against 206; passing the symbol to the call without the local is worse still, because GCC then derives the argument by subtracting 52 from the folded address. The deck scan must be an explicit pointer walk with its own counter. The array index form builds the same 206 but swaps the induction variables, putting the counter in a0 and the pointer in v1 and filling the delay slot of the preceding branch with the counter init rather than the %hi of the deck base. D_8009B398 and D_8009B3A4 are volatile, which is already recorded in src/game and is why every test reloads them.
